challenges.title: AI vs ML Quick Check
challenges.description: Which statement correctly distinguishes AI and ML?

choices.text: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data
ML is broader than AI and contains AI as a subset
AI and ML are unrelated fields
AI only works with robots, while ML only works with text

challenges.hint: Think about parent field vs subset.

solution.code: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: AI is the umbrella discipline that includes multiple approaches, and machine learning is one of those approaches.
steps.code: AI is the broader field; ML is a subset focused on learning from data

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: In everyday conversations, "AI" often refers to generative systems, but the field also includes planning, search, and robotics.

challenges.title: Structured or Unstructured?
challenges.description: A table with fixed columns for age, salary, and city is an example of:

choices.text: Structured data
Unstructured data
Streaming-only data
Synthetic data only

challenges.hint: Rows/columns with consistent schema indicate structure.

solution.code: Structured data

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: Structured data.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: Tabular records with fixed columns follow a predefined schema, which is the definition of structured data.
steps.code: Structured data

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: Most production ML systems combine structured tables with unstructured signals like text or images.

challenges.title: Feature or Label?
challenges.description: In a spam classifier, the email text is the input and spam/not-spam is the output. What is the output called?

choices.text: Label
Feature
Model
Dataset

challenges.hint: Features are inputs; labels are targets.

solution.code: Label

steps.title: Correct Solution
steps.explanation: The correct answer is: Label.

steps.title: Why
steps.explanation: The output the model must predict is the target variable, which in supervised learning is called the label.
steps.code: Label

steps.title: Curiosity
steps.explanation: A strong feature-label definition early in a project prevents many downstream data and evaluation mistakes.

challenges.title: Learning Type Match
challenges.description: Clustering customer records without known target values is:

choices.text: Reinforcement learning

Transfer learning
Supervised learning

solution.code: Unsupervised learning

steps.title: Curiosity
